# Climate Change and Floral Visual Traits 

```{r}
library(piecewiseSEM)
library(dplyr)
library(MuMIn)
library(MASS)

df_complete <- readr::read_csv(
  here::here("pollinator_traits_dataset.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
```

Initial attempt was made to fit Generalized Linear Mixed Effect Model with Individual_id and Block as random effects, but this resulted in convergence issues. Models with just species as random effects yielded similar results.

First, individual pollinator visitation models with abiotic treatments and traits were made. Step-wise selection was then conducted for these models to identify the significant abiotic factors and traits. Backward elimination was used as forward elimination simply resulted in a model with the same formula as the initial models.

```{r}
### Abiotic Factors Only Model
af_pv_model <- MASS::glm.nb(Pollinator ~ nutrient.x * water.x * Species + N_nutrient + N_water, data = df_complete)

### Traits Only Model
traits_pv_model <- MASS::glm.nb(Pollinator ~ Plant_height_cm + sqrt_No_of_flowers + log_Floral_area_mm2 + Bee_chromatic_contrast + Fly_chromatic_contrast + Achromatic_contrast + Total_brightness + log_Chroma + Hue, data = df_complete)

## Step-Wise Selection----
af_backward_step_model <- MASS::stepAIC(af_pv_model, direction = "backward")
traits_backward_step_model <- MASS::stepAIC(traits_pv_model, direction = "backward")
```

Two "complete" pollinator visitation models were made. One model contained all abiotic factors and traits while the other only contained those parameters which passed the step-wise selection from the individual models.

```{r}
# Complete Model
cpv_model <- MASS::glm.nb(Pollinator ~ nutrient.x * water.x * Species + Plant_height_cm + sqrt_No_of_flowers + log_Floral_area_mm2 + Bee_chromatic_contrast + Fly_chromatic_contrast + Achromatic_contrast + Total_brightness + log_Chroma + Hue + N_nutrient + N_water, data = df_complete)

# Model based on backward selection of individual abiotic factors and traits model
cpv_s_model <- MASS::glm.nb(Pollinator ~ nutrient.x + water.x + Species + nutrient.x:water.x + sqrt_No_of_flowers + log_Floral_area_mm2 + Bee_chromatic_contrast + Fly_chromatic_contrast + Achromatic_contrast + log_Chroma, data = df_complete)

# Step-wise selection
cpv_backward_step_model <- MASS::stepAIC(cpv_model, direction = "backward")
cpvs_backward_step_model <- MASS::stepAIC(cpv_s_model, direction = "backward")
```

Surprisingly, comparing both step models using AIC shows that the step-model made using the complete model has the lower AIC value (927.9378 vs 946.2106). Hence the formula of the complete step-model was chosen as the candidate for the downstream SEM.

```{r}
> AIC(cpv_backward_step_model, cpvs_backward_step_model)

> formula(cpv_backward_step_model) # Pollinator ~ nutrient.x + water.x + Species + log_Floral_area_mm2 + Bee_chromatic_contrast + Fly_chromatic_contrast + Achromatic_contrast + Total_brightness + nutrient.x:water.x + nutrient.x:Species + water.x:Species
```

For the first SEM model, made individual linear models of the traits~treatments for upstream and the complete model for the downstream as previously mentioned. Following this, the complete SEM model was fitted using *psem*.

```{r}
## Upstream ----
PH_model <- lm(Plant_height_cm ~ nutrient.x * water.x * Species, data = df_complete)
FN_model <- lm(sqrt_No_of_flowers ~ nutrient.x * water.x * Species, data = df_complete)
FA_model <- lm(log_Floral_area_mm2 ~ nutrient.x * water.x * Species, data = df_complete)
BCC_model <- lm(Bee_chromatic_contrast ~ nutrient.x * water.x * Species, data = df_complete)
FCC_model <- lm(Fly_chromatic_contrast ~ nutrient.x * water.x * Species, data = df_complete)
ACC_model <- lm(Achromatic_contrast ~ nutrient.x * water.x * Species, data = df_complete)
TB_model <- lm(Total_brightness ~ nutrient.x * water.x * Species, data = df_complete)
CH_model <- lm(log_Chroma ~ nutrient.x * water.x * Species, data = df_complete)
H_model <- lm(Hue ~ nutrient.x * water.x * Species, data = df_complete)

## Downstream ----
# based on formula(cpv_backward_step_model)
PV_model <- MASS::glm.nb(Pollinator ~ nutrient.x + water.x + Species + log_Floral_area_mm2 + Bee_chromatic_contrast + Fly_chromatic_contrast + Achromatic_contrast + Total_brightness + nutrient.x:water.x + nutrient.x:Species + water.x:Species, data = df_complete)

# Through correlation matrix, it was identified that BCC~FCC and ACC~TB are correlated pairs with r > 0.7

## SEM ----
sem_mod <- piecewiseSEM::psem(PH_model,FN_model, FA_model, BCC_model, FCC_model, ACC_model, TB_model, CH_model, H_model, PV_model, Bee_chromatic_contrast %~~% Fly_chromatic_contrast, Achromatic_contrast %~~% Total_brightness, data = df_complete)
summary(sem_mod, standardize = "none")
```

Both the AIC (9394.684) and fischerC (821.887, p = 0) were high. So used *dSep()* to identify colinear traits and adjusted the formula.

```{r}
### Separate model accounting dsep ----

sem_mod2 <- piecewiseSEM::psem(PH_model,FN_model, FA_model, BCC_model, FCC_model,
ACC_model, TB_model, CH_model, H_model, PV_model, Bee_chromatic_contrast %~~% Fly_chromatic_contrast, Achromatic_contrast %~~% Total_brightness, sqrt_No_of_flowers %~~% Plant_height_cm, log_Floral_area_mm2 %~~% Plant_height_cm, log_Floral_area_mm2 %~~% sqrt_No_of_flowers, Hue %~~% log_Floral_area_mm2, Achromatic_contrast %~~% Bee_chromatic_contrast, Total_brightness %~~% Bee_chromatic_contrast, log_Chroma %~~% Bee_chromatic_contrast, Hue %~~% Bee_chromatic_contrast, Achromatic_contrast %~~% Fly_chromatic_contrast, log_Chroma %~~% Fly_chromatic_contrast, Hue %~~% Fly_chromatic_contrast, log_Chroma %~~% Achromatic_contrast, Hue %~~% Achromatic_contrast, Hue %~~% Total_brightness, Hue %~~% log_Chroma, data = df_complete)
```

While the AIC stayed the same, the fischerC value drastically reduced (45.318, p = 0.5) suggesting a better fit. Given the *summary()* did not work with (standardize = "scale"), this parameter was set to "none" but this resulted in unstandardized coefficients. Due to this, the data was scaled prior to fitted the next SEM model.

```{r}
df_scaled <- df_complete
cont_vars <- c("Plant_height_cm", "sqrt_No_of_flowers", "log_Floral_area_mm2",
               "Bee_chromatic_contrast", "Fly_chromatic_contrast", 
               "Achromatic_contrast", "Total_brightness", 
               "log_Chroma", "Hue")

df_scaled[cont_vars] <- lapply(df_scaled[cont_vars], function(x) as.numeric(scale(x)))

#### Upstream ----
PH_model_scaled <- lm(Plant_height_cm ~ nutrient.x * water.x * Species, data = df_scaled)
FN_model_scaled <- lm(sqrt_No_of_flowers ~ nutrient.x * water.x * Species, data = df_scaled)
FA_model_scaled <- lm(log_Floral_area_mm2 ~ nutrient.x * water.x * Species, data = df_scaled)
BCC_model_scaled <- lm(Bee_chromatic_contrast ~ nutrient.x * water.x * Species, data = df_scaled)
FCC_model_scaled <- lm(Fly_chromatic_contrast ~ nutrient.x * water.x * Species, data = df_scaled)
ACC_model_scaled <- lm(Achromatic_contrast ~ nutrient.x * water.x * Species, data = df_scaled)
TB_model_scaled <- lm(Total_brightness ~ nutrient.x * water.x * Species, data = df_scaled)
CH_model_scaled <- lm(log_Chroma ~ nutrient.x * water.x * Species, data = df_scaled)
H_model_scaled <- lm(Hue ~ nutrient.x * water.x * Species, data = df_scaled)

#### Downstream ----
PV_model_scaled <- MASS::glm.nb(Pollinator ~ nutrient.x + water.x + Species + log_Floral_area_mm2 + Bee_chromatic_contrast + Fly_chromatic_contrast + Achromatic_contrast + Total_brightness + nutrient.x:water.x + nutrient.x:Species + water.x:Species, data = df_scaled)

#### SEM ----
sem_mod2_scaled <- piecewiseSEM::psem(PH_model_scaled,FN_model_scaled, FA_model_scaled, BCC_model_scaled, FCC_model_scaled, ACC_model_scaled, TB_model_scaled, CH_model_scaled, H_model_scaled, PV_model_scaled, Bee_chromatic_contrast %~~% Fly_chromatic_contrast, Achromatic_contrast %~~% Total_brightness, sqrt_No_of_flowers %~~% Plant_height_cm, log_Floral_area_mm2 %~~% Plant_height_cm, log_Floral_area_mm2 %~~% sqrt_No_of_flowers, Hue %~~% log_Floral_area_mm2, Achromatic_contrast %~~% Bee_chromatic_contrast, Total_brightness %~~% Bee_chromatic_contrast, log_Chroma %~~% Bee_chromatic_contrast, Hue %~~% Bee_chromatic_contrast, Achromatic_contrast %~~% Fly_chromatic_contrast, log_Chroma %~~% Fly_chromatic_contrast, Hue %~~% Fly_chromatic_contrast, log_Chroma %~~% Achromatic_contrast, Hue %~~% Achromatic_contrast, Hue %~~% Total_brightness, Hue %~~% log_Chroma, data = df_scaled)
```

This yielded a model of similar fischerC value (45.318 ; p = 0.501) but much lower AIC (4250.322) alongside providing standardized coefficients.

However, scaling of the continuous variables enabled the usage of Generalized linear mixed effects models for pollinator visitation which was previously not possible with the unscaled data. For model selection, the *dredge()* from the MuMIn package was used as the *MASS::stepAIC()* is not compatible with glmer.nb() models. 

```{r}
### Model Selection ----
### Abiotic Factors Only Model
af_pv_model_scaled <- glmer.nb(Pollinator ~ nutrient.x * water.x * Species + N_nutrient + N_water + (1|Block) + (1|Individual_id), data = df_scaled)
### Traits Only Model
traits_pv_model_scaled <- glmer.nb(Pollinator ~ Plant_height_cm + sqrt_No_of_flowers + log_Floral_area_mm2 + Bee_chromatic_contrast + Fly_chromatic_contrast + Achromatic_contrast + Total_brightness + log_Chroma + Hue + (1|Block) + (1|Individual_id), data = df_scaled)

## Dredging ----
options(na.action = "na.fail")
af_modelset <- dredge(af_pv_model_scaled)
traits_modelset <- dredge(traits_pv_model_scaled)
af_bestmodel <- get.models(af_modelset, 1)[[1]]
traits_bestmodel <- get.models(traits_modelset, 1)[[1]]
af_bestmodel # Formula: Pollinator ~ N_nutrient + N_water + nutrient.x + Species + water.x + (1 | Block) + (1 | Individual_id) + nutrient.x:water.x
traits_bestmodel # Formula: Pollinator ~ Achromatic_contrast + Bee_chromatic_contrast + Fly_chromatic_contrast + log_Chroma + log_Floral_area_mm2 + sqrt_No_of_flowers + (1 |Block) + (1 | Individual_id)

### Upstream ----
PH_model_scaled <- lmer(Plant_height_cm ~ nutrient.x * water.x * Species + (1 | Individual_id), data = df_scaled)
FN_model_scaled <- lmer(sqrt_No_of_flowers ~ nutrient.x * water.x * Species + (1 | Individual_id), data = df_scaled)
FA_model_scaled <- lmer(log_Floral_area_mm2 ~ nutrient.x * water.x * Species + (1 | Individual_id), data = df_scaled)
BCC_model_scaled <- lmer(Bee_chromatic_contrast ~ nutrient.x * water.x * Species + (1 | Individual_id), data = df_scaled)
FCC_model_scaled <- lmer(Fly_chromatic_contrast ~ nutrient.x * water.x * Species + (1 | Individual_id), data = df_scaled)
ACC_model_scaled <- lmer(Achromatic_contrast ~ nutrient.x * water.x * Species + (1 | Individual_id), data = df_scaled)
TB_model_scaled <- lmer(Total_brightness ~ nutrient.x * water.x * Species + (1 | Individual_id), data = df_scaled)
CH_model_scaled <- lmer(log_Chroma ~ nutrient.x * water.x * Species + (1 | Individual_id), data = df_scaled)
H_model_scaled <- lmer(Hue ~ nutrient.x * water.x * Species + (1 | Individual_id), data = df_scaled)

#### Downstream ----
PV_model_scaled <- glmer.nb(Pollinator ~ nutrient.x + water.x + Species + nutrient.x:water.x + Achromatic_contrast +Bee_chromatic_contrast + Fly_chromatic_contrast + log_Chroma + log_Floral_area_mm2 + sqrt_No_of_flowers +(1 |Block) + (1 | Individual_id), data = df_scaled)

#### SEM ----

sem_mod3_scaled <- piecewiseSEM::psem(PH_model_scaled,FN_model_scaled, FA_model_scaled, BCC_model_scaled, FCC_model_scaled,
ACC_model_scaled, TB_model_scaled, CH_model_scaled, H_model_scaled, PV_model_scaled, Bee_chromatic_contrast %~~% Fly_chromatic_contrast,
Achromatic_contrast %~~% Total_brightness, sqrt_No_of_flowers %~~% Plant_height_cm,log_Floral_area_mm2 %~~% Plant_height_cm,log_Floral_area_mm2 %~~% sqrt_No_of_flowers, Hue %~~% log_Floral_area_mm2,Achromatic_contrast %~~% Bee_chromatic_contrast,Total_brightness %~~% Bee_chromatic_contrast,log_Chroma %~~% Bee_chromatic_contrast,Hue %~~% Bee_chromatic_contrast,Achromatic_contrast %~~% Fly_chromatic_contrast,log_Chroma %~~% Fly_chromatic_contrast,Hue %~~% Fly_chromatic_contrast,log_Chroma %~~% Achromatic_contrast,Hue %~~% Achromatic_contrast,Hue %~~% Total_brightness,Hue %~~% log_Chroma, data = df_scaled)
```

This yielded a SEM model of slightly higher AIC (4789) and fischerC (53.744, p = 0.149) but could be considered superior to the previous model due to its integration of random effects. It should be noted this model received multiple "boundary (singular) fit" and convergence warnings while the previous models received none. This could be due to the limited sample size and near-zero variance by the random effects.

Simply to consider all options, a SEM model with scaled data where random effects were only integrated in the upstream models while the pollinator visitation model was left without random effects was fitted. 

```{r}
## SEM (With scaled data and random effect only in upstream) ----

### Upstream ----
PH_model_scaled <- lmer(Plant_height_cm ~ nutrient.x * water.x * Species + (1 | Individual_id), data = df_scaled)
FN_model_scaled <- lmer(sqrt_No_of_flowers ~ nutrient.x * water.x * Species + (1 | Individual_id), data = df_scaled)
FA_model_scaled <- lmer(log_Floral_area_mm2 ~ nutrient.x * water.x * Species + (1 | Individual_id), data = df_scaled)
BCC_model_scaled <- lmer(Bee_chromatic_contrast ~ nutrient.x * water.x * Species + (1 | Individual_id), data = df_scaled)
FCC_model_scaled <- lmer(Fly_chromatic_contrast ~ nutrient.x * water.x * Species + (1 | Individual_id), data = df_scaled)
ACC_model_scaled <- lmer(Achromatic_contrast ~ nutrient.x * water.x * Species + (1 | Individual_id), data = df_scaled)
TB_model_scaled <- lmer(Total_brightness ~ nutrient.x * water.x * Species + (1 | Individual_id), data = df_scaled)
CH_model_scaled <- lmer(log_Chroma ~ nutrient.x * water.x * Species + (1 | Individual_id), data = df_scaled)
H_model_scaled <- lmer(Hue ~ nutrient.x * water.x * Species + (1 | Individual_id), data = df_scaled)

#### Downstream ----
PV_model_scaled <- MASS::glm.nb(Pollinator ~ nutrient.x + water.x + Species + log_Floral_area_mm2 + Bee_chromatic_contrast + Fly_chromatic_contrast + Achromatic_contrast + Total_brightness + nutrient.x:water.x + nutrient.x:Species + water.x:Species, data = df_scaled)

#### SEM ----
sem_mod4_scaled <- piecewiseSEM::psem(PH_model_scaled,FN_model_scaled, FA_model_scaled, BCC_model_scaled, FCC_model_scaled, ACC_model_scaled, TB_model_scaled, CH_model_scaled, H_model_scaled, PV_model_scaled, Bee_chromatic_contrast %~~% Fly_chromatic_contrast, Achromatic_contrast %~~% Total_brightness, sqrt_No_of_flowers %~~% Plant_height_cm, log_Floral_area_mm2 %~~% Plant_height_cm, log_Floral_area_mm2 %~~% sqrt_No_of_flowers, Hue %~~% log_Floral_area_mm2, Achromatic_contrast %~~% Bee_chromatic_contrast, Total_brightness %~~% Bee_chromatic_contrast, log_Chroma %~~% Bee_chromatic_contrast,Hue %~~% Bee_chromatic_contrast,Achromatic_contrast %~~% Fly_chromatic_contrast,log_Chroma %~~% Fly_chromatic_contrast,Hue %~~% Fly_chromatic_contrast,log_Chroma %~~% Achromatic_contrast,Hue %~~% Achromatic_contrast,Hue %~~% Total_brightness,Hue %~~% log_Chroma, data = df_scaled)
```

The final model had a AIC value of 4748.011 and fischerC of 49.406 (p = 0.339).  To conclude the SEM model with scaled data and without random effects is the most parsimonious and "well-fitted" while the SEM model with scaled data and random effects in both upstream and downstream can be considered more "statistically-appropriate" while still having its fair share of drawbacks as mentioned above.
